mcqs.question: A particle executes simple harmonic motion described by x = A cos(ωt + φ). At t = 0 the displacement is zero and the velocity is maximum in the positive direction. What is the value of the phase constant φ?
mcqs.explanation: From x = A cos(ωt + φ), x(0)=0 gives cos φ = 0 ⇒ φ = ±π/2. Velocity v = -Aω sin(ωt + φ); v(0) must be +Aω (maximum positive). Hence -Aω sin φ = +Aω ⇒ sin φ = -1 ⇒ φ = -π/2. Option C is correct; the other values either give non‑zero displacement at t=0 or give velocity in the wrong direction.

mcqs.question: A mass attached to a spring is pulled to a displacement +A and released from rest. Which of the following displacement‑time graphs correctly represents its subsequent motion?

options.A: A sine curve that starts from the origin (x = 0) and rises.
options.B: A cosine curve that starts at the maximum positive displacement (+A) and then decreases.
options.C: A cosine curve that starts at the maximum negative displacement (‑A).
options.D: A sine curve that starts at the maximum positive displacement (+A).

mcqs.answer: A cosine curve that starts at the maximum positive displacement (+A) and then decreases.
mcqs.explanation: When released from rest at +A, the displacement follows x = A cos(ωt) because at t = 0, cos 0 = 1 giving x = +A and the velocity (proportional to -sin ωt) is zero. Hence the graph is a cosine curve beginning at the top (+A) and moving downward. Option B matches this; the other options describe incorrect initial conditions.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines simple harmonic motion (SHM)?

options.A: SHM occurs whenever the net force on a particle is proportional to its velocity.
options.B: SHM occurs when the restoring force on a particle is directly proportional to its displacement and directed toward the equilibrium position.
options.C: SHM is the motion of a particle when its kinetic energy remains constant.
options.D: SHM happens only for motions that involve circular trajectories.

mcqs.answer: SHM occurs when the restoring force on a particle is directly proportional to its displacement and directed toward the equilibrium position.
mcqs.explanation: The defining feature of SHM is a restoring force (or acceleration) that obeys F = –k x (or a = –ω² x), i.e., it is proportional to displacement and opposite in direction. Option B states this correctly. Option A confuses damping with SHM, C is false because kinetic energy varies, and D is unrelated.

mcqs.question: A 0.5 kg block is attached to a horizontal spring of force constant 200 N m⁻¹. The block is displaced 5 cm to the right and released. In which direction does the restoring force act immediately after release?
mcqs.explanation: The restoring force of a spring is given by F = –k x. Here x = +0.05 m (rightward), so F = –200 × 0.05 = –10 N, i.e., 10 N directed opposite to the displacement, i.e., to the left. Hence option B is correct; the other directions do not oppose the displacement.

mcqs.question: Two students write the displacement of a particle in SHM as (i) x = A cos(ωt + φ) and (ii) x = A sin(ωt + φ). For a motion that starts from the equilibrium position moving in the positive direction, which of the following statements is true?

options.A: Equation (i) with φ = 0 correctly describes the motion, while equation (ii) cannot.
options.B: Equation (ii) with φ = 0 correctly describes the motion, while equation (i) cannot.
options.C: Both equations describe the same motion if φ is chosen appropriately.
options.D: Neither equation can represent the described motion.

mcqs.answer: Both equations describe the same motion if φ is chosen appropriately.
mcqs.explanation: Starting from equilibrium (x = 0) with positive velocity requires sin (ωt + φ) = 0 and cos (ωt + φ) = 1 at t = 0. This is achieved by (i) with φ = –π/2 (cos(–π/2)=0, velocity positive) or by (ii) with φ = 0 (sin 0 = 0, velocity positive). Thus, by selecting suitable phase constants, both forms represent the same physical motion. Options A and B ignore the role of φ, and D is false.

mcqs.question: For a particle executing SHM with amplitude A and angular frequency ω, which of the following relationships is always true?

options.A: Maximum speed v_max = ω A and maximum acceleration a_max = ω A
options.B: Maximum speed v_max = ω A and maximum acceleration a_max = ω² A
options.C: Maximum speed v_max = ω² A and maximum acceleration a_max = ω A
options.D: Maximum speed v_max = A/ω and maximum acceleration a_max = A/ω²

mcqs.answer: Maximum speed v_max = ω A and maximum acceleration a_max = ω² A
mcqs.explanation: In SHM, x = A cos(ωt + φ). Differentiating gives v = –Aω sin(ωt + φ) → |v|_max = Aω. Differentiating again gives a = –Aω² cos(ωt + φ) → |a|_max = Aω². Therefore option B correctly states both maxima. Options A, C, and D misuse the powers of ω.

mcqs.question: In the SHM expression x = A cos(ωt + φ), the term φ is called the:
mcqs.explanation: The symbol φ (phi) represents the phase constant (or initial phase) which determines the starting point of the motion on the cosine curve. Amplitude is A, angular frequency is ω, and period is 2π/ω. Hence option C is correct.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes the velocity‑time graph for a particle undergoing simple harmonic motion?

options.A: It is a sine wave that is in phase with the displacement graph.
options.B: It is a cosine wave that is 90° out of phase with the displacement graph.
options.C: It is a straight line passing through the origin.
options.D: It is a cosine wave that is in phase with the displacement graph.

mcqs.answer: It is a cosine wave that is 90° out of phase with the displacement graph.
mcqs.explanation: For SHM, if displacement is x = A cos(ωt + φ), velocity is v = –Aω sin(ωt + φ), which is a sine (or cosine shifted by –90°) and therefore 90° out of phase with displacement. Option B captures this relationship. Option A incorrectly states they are in phase, C is wrong because velocity varies sinusoidally, and D repeats the displacement phase.
